course_description:
Principal hazards of MRI environment and its effects on the human body and equipment. Physiological monitoring strategies examined from the origin of signals to integration with the imaging system. Considerations in planning for MR installations are reviewed.

Patient Monitoring and MR Safety deals with two broad areas within magnetic resonance technology. Firstly, the techniques used to monitor patients remotely while undergoing an MR examination are discussed. The relevant physiology and technology of the major monitoring modalities are described and the considerations unique to the MR environment are dealt with.

Secondly, hazards due to the nature of MR imaging are reviewed and the rationale for various safety limitations on imaging parameters are examined. The student should also be equipped to deal with the various issues involved in siting and commissioning an MR imaging suite by the completion of these modules.

course_aims: The course aims to give students in-depth understanding of the hardware components of MRI systems. We will focus on the superconducting magnet, gradient and radio frequency coils, and shim coils, and consider their function, how they are designed, and where relevant, discuss how these are fabricated and put together to form a functioning system. We outline the limitations of each component and how they may influence data acquisition and ultimately image quality. We finish by describing the key considerations to be made for the safe operation of MRI systems.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the physical principles and biological effects of MRI electromagnetic fields, including the static field (B₀), RF field (B₁), and gradient fields, and their implications for patient and staff safety.

Apply MRI safety screening and risk-assessment procedures to determine patient eligibility for MRI, including the evaluation of implants, pregnancy, foreign bodies, tattoos, and prior surgical history.

Interpret and apply international MRI device labelling standards (MR Safe, MR Conditional, MR Unsafe) and manufacturer specifications to make evidence-based decisions for scanning patients with implants and medical devices.
Implement safe MRI operational practices in relation to magnet siting, access control, zoning, emergency procedures, quench events, and cryogen hazards.
Safely manage gadolinium-based contrast agents, including agent selection, dose administration, recognition of adverse reactions, and management of gadolinium retention risks.
Perform and interpret physiological monitoring in the MRI environment

Demonstrate professional and legal accountability in MRI practice by applying institutional policies, regulatory frameworks, and the roles of MRI safety personnel to ensure patient, staff, and facility safety.
